reading_workflow.detail: The whole page was inspected once for layout. Both native-dimension overlapping halves were read once line by line, including agreed words and the blank lower portion. Twenty-one text baselines count: heading; objects heading; two circle lines; Sommets and the parenthetical continuation; final circle line; two condition lines; diagram annotation; catalogue heading; seven numbered item baselines; one interlinear replacement baseline; closing line; folio. The eight diagram vertices, all edges/arrowheads, two upper braces, two catalogue braces, two vertical double arrows and short underline were inspected separately. No OCR, web research or TeX compilation was used.
reading_workflow.crop_method: Each first crop is the original saved enhanced PNG rectangle; same-dimension quality95 JPEG proxies were used only for display. Changes cite original rectangles. Second-reading boxes may be tighter subrectangles.
reading_workflow.mathematics: No independent mathematical proposition was evaluated; checks is intentionally empty.

changes.ink: The angular upper cap, short rightward turn and broad lower return match the calligraphic T forms after S, D and SD on this same sheet. The top live glyph is separate from the cancelled block to its left; its letter strokes are not hidden by that cancellation.

Two close upright strokes are joined at the top; a distinct crossbar projects right around mid-height, and a bent foot projects right below. The crossbar favors t, while the doubled outline leaves the alphabet unresolved.

The initial s is visibly shorter than the following doubled upright and than the large S in the left diamond. The following glyph repeats the middle crossbar and rightward foot of the top right glyph.
A small lower loop and ascending staff form d. The following doubled upright again has a middle crossbar and a lower right foot; its t-versus-L reading remains explicit.
The first s is small, followed by the loop-and-staff d. The last tall sign repeats the crossbar and bent foot seen at the other three vertices.

changes.place: Diamonds: origin of the upper middle connecting arrow
changes.ink: The thin stroke begins immediately above D followed by the calligraphic letter, curves slightly downward to the right, and ends in a clear arrowhead before the right diamond's left vertex. The short S-to-D line farther left ends without a head and does not continue into this arrow.
After the d loop and staff, the final low joined stroke is strongly flattened. It does not separate cleanly enough into an e loop or a u trough to settle de against du.
Before the m run there is a separate initial s curve, then the low joined u and r strokes. The word begins well before the m; those prefix strokes are live and continuous with the word.
A small dark point lies just after the closing parenthesis, but its short tail is not securely distinguished from the mottled paper. The comma is retained only in doubt.
The separate rule begins left of the first a and stops beneath the middle portion of amalgamation, while several letters continue clearly to the right. The rule does not extend under the whole word.

changes.place: Catalogue item 5: cancelled wording and possible opening parenthesis
changes.ink: A densely cancelled short group follows recollage. Farther right, a curved descending stroke precedes surviving tall letter parts, and the horizontal strike continues through that old line. It may be an opening parenthesis after avec; the words and the position of this curve remain doubtful. The closing parenthesis at the far right remains live.
Sans gommage! is written on a higher baseline above the crossed-out phrase. Its g descenders and final exclamation mark are distinct from the horizontal cancellation below.

changes.h: Two vertical double arrows between rows 2 and 3 and between rows 4 and 5.
changes.ink: Both vertical strokes have visible heads at both ends. The first is beside the space following row 2; the second starts at the height of row 4 and ends beside row 5, rather than below row 5.
The short group after gommage has the loop-and-staff d and a low finishing stroke; no separate terminal s curve is visible before the gap to cercles.
The group between gommage and cercles ends after a short low stroke following d; there is no further s-shaped turn before the space.
After the tall t, the remaining run is longer than -ernes and has an accent above its beginning, followed by the low joined -ieurs ending. The final word is intérieurs.

An open-topped 4 has a horizontal joining stroke and a long right upright; the following 1 has an oblique entry and a long descending shaft. These thin, separate figures are at the foot of the sheet, away from the main handwriting.

This is a medium-confidence resolution from visible letter shapes, not from a presumed diagrammatic meaning.

notes.text: This sheet gives an objects list, a paired diagram of symbolic vertices, and a seven-item catalogue. The page does not state a proposition whose proof or numerical value was checked in this first reading.

The four doubled right-hand glyphs are visually related, but this repetition has not been used to choose an alphabet by expected mathematical meaning. The t versus blackboard L alternatives remain explicit.

The interlinear replacement is legible. The crossed-out phrase and a possible opening parenthesis beneath it remain doubtful; no grammatical repair has been supplied to balance an uncertain old parenthesis.
The bottom number is 41 in a separate thin hand and is recorded as a margin entry. No date is visible in the source handwriting on this sheet.
Faint regular rows and other pale show-through marks do not belong to the dark front-side manuscript. They have not been turned into source words, illegibility marks, or alternative readings.
The source underline is shorter than the word. Its visible span is drawn rather than silently extended to every letter.
